small_guidance:
- The LN+GELU+scale kernel is fine but trivial; the conv_transpose3d is dominating runtime (fast_p ~0.23 means ~4x slower than baseline). Tuning BLOCK_C/num_warps on the LN kernel won't help — only ~1% of total time is in that kernel.
- If keeping current structure, at least add `@triton.autotune` over `num_warps ∈ {1,2,4}` for the LN kernel keyed on C, but this saves microseconds at best.
- The real issue is the unfused `nn.ConvTranspose3d` call inside forward — no amount of LN tuning will close the gap.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile), compute the input×weight outer product and scatter-add into the output grid using stride/padding/output_padding index math. Output shape is (32, 64, 32, 64, 64) — large but tractable.
- Layout the output as channels-last (NDHWC) so the LN epilogue reduction across C=64 stays contiguous and coalesces. Allocate the conv-transpose output directly in NDHWC.
- Fuse the bias add into the conv-transpose epilogue, then run LN+GELU+scale as a second kernel over the channels-last tensor (LN reduces only 64 elements per row — can be a single warp per row). Alternative: a two-pass design where pass 1 computes the conv-transpose output + per-row sum/sumsq atomically, pass 2 applies LN+GELU+scale; but a simpler split (conv-transpose kernel → existing LN kernel) is sufficient since LN cost is small.
